# Live GitHub runs, 2026-10-14

Repository `dilipna/furnace-demo-f1` (public), App `furnace-dev-dilipna` (id in `.env`,
installation 171233745, selected repositories: this one only). Every attempt is kept.

## Attempt 1 (05:08 UTC, code eb5f8a4): INCOMPLETE, stopped at Forge

`attempt-1/live_run.{json,md}`. App check and branch heads passed. Forge validated its change
set in the sandbox (13 files), then opening the draft PR failed: `POST /git/trees` 403
"Resource not accessible by integration". Nothing was written to the repository.

Cause, confirmed with a probe using the same PR-scoped token (tree objects only, unreferenced,
no branch or ref changed): a normal file → 201; a file under `.github/workflows/` → 403.
GitHub needs the separate `workflows` permission for those paths. The mock GitHub used in the
tests did not model it, so this was first seen live.

Fix (40d41a3): Furnace still does not request `workflows`; Forge commits the other files and
puts the workflow file in the PR description for the reviewer to add.

## Attempt 2

Recorded in `live_run.{json,md}` beside this file, after the fix, same repository and App.
(05:11 UTC, code 3456656, clean): **PASS**, every step.

| step | result |
|---|---|
| Forge | draft PR https://github.com/dilipna/furnace-demo-f1/pull/1 (`furnace/forge-bb4d918` → main), 13 files validated in the sandbox; the workflow file is in the PR description, not committed |
| R1 PR | https://github.com/dilipna/furnace-demo-f1/pull/2 (`r1-request-id` → main, head 0a637d7) |
| Guard | check run 115692708323 on 0a637d7: **failure**, "2 regressions found: prompt_prefix_stable, chat_perf_gate". 7 of 8 checks selected. Perf gate: geometric-mean TTFT 72.7 → 501.7 ms (+590.0%, 90% interval +557.4 to +624.3), BLOCK; prefix-cache hit 98% → 0%; p95 advisory +851.8%. Judge SKIP (no key, not a pass); citation check 1/34 vs 0/34 on base (at its floor, says nothing about quality). 97 s |
| Repair | first strategy (`move_dynamic_to_suffix`) rejected: +36.1% vs main (90% interval +27.8 to +45.1), BLOCK. Second (`move_dynamic_to_log`) accepted: -1.6% vs main (90% interval -9.1 to +6.6), with the PR at +593.5% (72.4 → 502.1 ms) in the same interleaved runs; draft PR https://github.com/dilipna/furnace-demo-f1/pull/3 (`furnace/repair-pr2-0a637d7` → `r1-request-id`). 210 s |
| Replays | Forge and repair run again on the same commits returned PRs #1 and #3 (`reused=True`). The repair replay re-measured: first strategy +46.7% (+44.4 to +49.1) BLOCK, accepted fix -0.7% (-4.5 to +3.4) |

One live trial (plus its replay) on a laptop GPU, not a rate; each figure comes from its own
step's interleaved runs (`live_run.json`, steps `guard`, `repair`, `replay_repair`). The GPU clock was not pinned for this run (a demonstration, not a
measurement campaign).

## Independent verification (05:20 UTC): **PASS**, 10/10

`verify.{json,md}`, read from GitHub and the local receiver, not from the run record:
permissions equal the manifest and the installation covers only this repository; Scan and
Guard tokens get 403 on writes; the check run is on the PR's head commit, by this App, with a
start, a completion and annotations on `app/prompts.py` (each changed hunk is annotated once
per failing check, so the two lines appear twice); both PRs are drafts by
`furnace-dev-dilipna[bot]` from `furnace/*` branches; `main` and `r1-request-id` unchanged;
one open Furnace PR per base; 3 real `pull_request` deliveries reached the receiver over HMAC
through the smee relay (outcomes: ignored, queued); a GitHub redelivery changed no rows;
unsigned, wrong-secret and tampered requests got 401.

The Guard runner was stopped during the run so the webhook-triggered job would not compete
for the GPU with the run's own Guard; that job was queued (outcome "queued").

## The webhook-queued job, run afterwards (05:2x UTC)

The real `pull_request` delivery had queued one `guard.pr` job (6e6731cc) for PR #2's head
0a637d7. With the runner started (Guard settings in its `.env`), it claimed the job and
**succeeded**: it found Furnace's completed check run 115692708323 on that head commit and
reused it (`reused: true`, conclusion failure) instead of opening a second one. So the event
path GitHub delivery → HMAC → job → runner is shown; a fresh Guard run triggered by a webhook
is not (the head had already been checked). `signatures: []` in the reused result, so no
repair job was enqueued (repair consent was also off).

# Held-out set 6: results and review (protocol `docs/scanner-eval-set6.md`)

Scanner frozen at 41ca529; five apps chosen by one pre-declared GitHub search
(`selection.md`); labels and expected findings committed in ebd5824 before any scan. Labels
by the developer agent, not independent. Three quantities, never combined:

| quantity | result | file |
|---|---|---|
| LLM call sites (first scan) | found **32/48** (67%, exact 95% CI 52-80%), precision **32/32** (CI 89-100%) | `rq1.md` (column "held-out set 6") |
| Blueprint findings | precision **39/77** (51%, CI 39-62%), recall **39/64** (61%, CI 48-73%) | `set6/findings.md` |
| Evidence links | **148/148** resolve (6 file-level) | `set6/citations.md` |

Per app, call sites: Soul-of-Waifu 24/27, BYO-LLM-WIKI 5/12, audiobook-creator 3/5,
mdflux 0/3, ps-fuzz 0/1. The pooled 32/48 is dominated by Soul-of-Waifu's 27 sites, which
are one pattern repeated (nine provider classes x three methods); the mean of per-app recall
is 0.38. Compared with sets 1-5 (first scans pooled 4/34), set 6 is higher; the sets are
different apps and are reported side by side, not pooled.

The headline point: every evidence link resolved while half of the emitted findings were
wrong. Link validity says nothing about finding correctness.

## Review of every disagreement (after the result; the numbers above are not changed)

Judged by the developer agent after seeing the output. "Label" = the pre-registered label or
its definition was wrong or too narrow; "scanner" = the scanner was wrong; "open" = defensible
either way.

**Missed call sites (16), all scanner:** raw HTTP chat requests (mdflux 3, Soul-of-Waifu's
Anthropic provider 3); LangChain chat models received as a function parameter or held in
`self.client` (BYO 7, ps-fuzz 1); Pydantic AI `Agent(...).run` (audiobook 2).

**Emitted, not expected (38):**
- Scanner, 32: `sec.tool_approval_boundary` on 28 functions that no model can call (ffmpeg,
  file saves, config writes, release scripts: audiobook 23, mdflux 4, ps-fuzz 1). The rule
  treats any side-effecting function as a tool. `eval.grounding_judge` on mdflux (no
  retrieval). BYO: `rel.fallback_gateway` and `eval.regression_suite` (it has explicit
  `max_retries=2` and Ragas evals, neither recognized). audiobook: `inf.prefix_instability`
  on a system message whose leading value is fixed per deployment (static analysis cannot
  tell; under the pre-declared definition the label stands).
- Label, 4: prompt constants whose names lack "prompt"/"instruction"/"system"
  (`_CROSSDOC_JUDGE`, `_REQUIREMENTS`, `_SKILL_JSON_SHAPE` in BYO; `ethical_compliance_template`
  in ps-fuzz). The naming rule in the labels was too narrow; the scanner was right.
- Open, 2: audiobook `inf.serving_baseline` (its default endpoint is a local LM Studio
  server: self-hosted, but not in the rule's engine list the labels mirrored); ps-fuzz
  `eval.grounding_judge` (its RAG-poisoning attack does retrieve; labeled as not RAG because
  it does not ground answers).

**Expected, not emitted (25):**
- Cascade from missed call sites, 8: every app-level rule needs an LLM call, so mdflux (0/3
  call sites) and ps-fuzz (0/1) lost timeout, fallback, eval, tracing and serving findings.
- Tools not recognized, 8 (BYO): LangChain `@tool` functions, and the MCP write path's
  approval gate.
- Prompts built inside functions, 8 (audiobook 7: f-string system prompts inside functions
  and Pydantic AI `system_prompt=`, and the prefix rules that depend on them) and 1 (BYO:
  the deep agent's `system_prompt=` constant).
- audiobook `obs.genai_tracing`, 1: scanner.

Re-scored with the four label corrections only (for orientation, not a result): precision
43/77, recall 43/68. The pre-registered numbers stand.

## What this says about the scanner

It is accurate where it fires on call sites (no false positive in 48 labeled sites) but
misses common constructs (raw HTTP, injected LangChain models, Pydantic AI, LangChain
tools), and each missed call site silently removes the app-level findings that depend on it.
Its tool rule is wrong in kind: it flags side-effecting functions that no model can invoke.
Neither is fixed here; a fix would be measured on a new held-out set (set 6 is now spent).

# Does uncertain or unsupported analysis widen the checks, or silently skip them? (2026-10-13)

Question (owner, 2026-10-13): when Guard's impact analysis cannot account for a change, does
it fall back to broader checks, or does it skip checks that matter? And does Scan say what it
could not read?

## Guard: verified by tests written before the fix

The documented rule was "an application-code change that maps to no fact selects the full
suite". It held only for *modified Python lines*. Seven tests were written against the code
at d2df18d (`packages/furnace/tests/test_impact.py`, section "uncertain or unsupported
analysis"); **six failed** (no fallback, and in five of them no category either, so nothing
but the always-on checks ran):

| change in the PR (on F1) | before (d2df18d) | after |
|---|---|---|
| an article in `docs/` that `app/retriever.py` loads (`(ROOT / "docs").glob("*.md")`) | category `docs`, nothing selected | full suite: "read by application code (app/retriever.py:28)" |
| a TypeScript file added under `app/` | skipped, no category | full suite: "source the analysis does not parse" |
| an unmodelled data file in the app (`app/data/thresholds.csv`) | skipped, no category | full suite: "a file the analysis does not model" |
| an added Python module that maps to no graph node | skipped (added files have no hunks) | full suite |
| a removed Python module that maps to no graph node | skipped | full suite |
| an app module that no longer parses | treated as removed nodes | full suite: "does not parse as Python" |
| CI workflow, an image, CHANGELOG (inert) | no fallback | no fallback (unchanged, the seventh test) |

A template the scanner models (`.j2`) is still targeted, not a fallback (its prompt node is
touched). Rule now (`guardian/impact.py`): a changed file is either mapped to graph nodes,
or known to be inert (tests, CI, repository metadata, images, docs nothing reads), or it
selects the full suite with the reason. "Read by application code" is a string-literal
heuristic on the file name or its directory; it errs toward a fallback, which only widens.

## Effect on results already reported

- RQ3 (13 F1 PR scenarios, `2026-10-06/rq3/`): selection recomputed under the new rule is
  identical in 13/13 scenarios (`docs_only` edits the README, which nothing reads). RQ3 never
  exercised the cases above, so its "targeted ran 46% of checks" is unchanged and says nothing
  about them.
- Held-out set 4 synthetic PRs (`external_validation.md` here vs `2026-10-12-reconcile/`): the
  Guard table is identical, 9/9 correct.

## Scan: what it could not read

Unchanged and verified: a repository whose source is in a language other than Python gets a
coverage box on the Blueprint naming the languages and their share, and an empty Blueprint
says "a coverage limit, not a clean bill of health". New: Python files the extractor skips
(syntax errors, Python 2, files over 2 MB) were silently dropped; they are now listed in the
scan's stats (`python_not_analyzed`) and in the same coverage box.

# Optimizer grid and independent confirmation (2026-10-13)

Design and decision rules fixed before any measurement (`docs/optimizer.md`; confirmation
rules added before the grid). Run by `bench/run_remaining_gpu.sh` after RQ5, 18:37-19:21 UTC.
Pre-run conditions `conditions/2026-10-13T183741Z.json`: on AC, vLLM image
`sha256:8a69ffad...`, measurement code clean at **6efebfd**, 780 MHz under the probe load.
(The 03:15 UTC attempt refused to start on battery, `conditions/2026-10-13T031547Z.json`; no
grid result exists from it.)

## Result: no change is recommended

- **Grid** (`optimizer/optimizer.md`): 5 of 8 configs feasible. Highest median SLO goodput:
  0.5B, prefix caching on, max-num-seqs 8, 8.34 req/s (range 7.37-8.34), against the
  baseline (0.5B, caching on, seqs 32) at 8.30 (7.36-8.37). The ranges overlap, so by the
  pre-declared rule the recommendation is **keep the baseline**. Infeasible: both 1.5B-AWQ
  configs with caching off (p95 TTFT about 1.1 s > 500 ms SLO) and 0.5B caching off seqs 8
  (facts quality not shown within the 5-point tolerance: -1.6, interval -7.8 to +4.7).
- **Independent confirmation** (`optimizer/confirm.md`; 8 fresh launches A B B A A B B A, new
  seeds): **inconclusive**. Goodput B vs A +3.8% (90% interval -8.8 to +18.2); p95 TTFT +1.0%
  (-6.7 to +9.5); quality facts +0.0 pts (-4.0 to +4.0), citations +0.0. No improvement is
  claimed.
- What the grid does show, as measured on this laptop: turning prefix caching off roughly
  halves goodput for the 0.5B model (4.4-4.7 vs 8.3 req/s) and pushes the 1.5B-AWQ model past
  the 500 ms p95 SLO; 1.5B-AWQ scores higher on both deterministic quality checks (facts
  85.7% vs 74.6%, citations 12.7% vs 0.0%) at about 77% of the 0.5B goodput with caching on.

## Clocks (not set; chosen by the driver)

| config | SM MHz, 3 runs |
|---|---|
| 0.5B caching on, seqs 8 / 32 (pick, baseline) | 780 / 780 |
| 1.5B-AWQ caching on, seqs 8 / 32 | 781-782 |
| 0.5B caching off, seqs 8 / 32 | 796-847 / 791-810 |
| 1.5B-AWQ caching off, seqs 8 / 32 | 1,421-1,644 / 1,349-1,621 |

All eight confirmation launches ran at 780 MHz. The driver raised the clock only for the
heaviest (caching-off) configs, which makes them look faster than they would at 780 MHz; they
were slower or infeasible anyway, so no conclusion depends on it. The pick and the baseline
were compared at the same clock, in the grid and in the confirmation.

## Limits

One GPU, one workload (W1), concurrency 8; quality is two deterministic checks, not judged
answer quality; the grid's three runs per config are consecutive on one container. Cost is
N/A (no $/GPU-hour on a self-hosted laptop).

## Operator activity during the run

File reads, greps, `git status`/`git log`, a directory comparison and one `python -c` that
printed a stored JSON field (about 0.1 s), between 18:40 and 19:10 UTC. No test, lint, build
or analysis script ran.

## Affected trials: the rule

Added 2026-10-13 ~00:55 UTC at the owner's direction, after trials 1-14 had been seen and
before trial 15 ran. It is a validity rule, not an analysis change.

1. **Definition.** A trial is *affected* if competing compute ran on the machine during the
   trial's window: a test run, lint/format/type check, build, Docker or sandbox job,
   benchmark, or analysis script that is not part of the trial. File reads, searches, text
   edits, git and status checks of about 2 s or less are not competing compute.
2. **Evidence, not results.** Whether a trial is affected is decided from a timestamped log
   of what ran (the session's command log, with each command's start and end), compared
   with the trial's start time and duration. The trial's verdict, change or interval is
   never consulted.
3. **Handling.** An affected trial stays in the record with its result
   (`validation/<set>.json`, `affected` lists it with the reason and evidence). It is left
   out of the primary tally and replaced by one more trial at the end of the same set, so the
   set reaches its planned count of unaffected trials. The report shows a second row with
   the affected trials included, so their effect on every figure is visible.
4. **Going forward.** No competing compute is run by the operator during the remaining
   trials, and each trial records the machine's CPU busy share while it ran (mean and largest
   1 s value) as supporting data; no rule uses that number.

# 2026-10-11: perf gate with 95% intervals (bench/run_gate_ci.sh)

Code: commit `6ee6cc1` (interval-based gate from `5e7c066`), working tree clean. Lab vLLM,
Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, RTX 3050 Ti laptop; SM clock 780 MHz in every run (the same clock as
the 2026-10-09 A/A, so the two are comparable). Unrelated containers (`wc26-mlops-*`,
`cal-api`) were running, as in earlier campaigns.

## gate_noise.md: VALID (12 trials, 34 requests per run)

On AC at start (pre-flight 22:58 UTC: "Best performance", not throttled) and at the end
(manifest: on AC, 90%, 80 W GPU limit); every trial took 52-55 s.

- Verdicts: PASS 7/12, INCONCLUSIVE 5/12, false WARN 0/12, false BLOCK 0/12.
- The 95% interval contained the true difference (0) in 12/12; median width 21.4 points.
- Largest A/A change: **+13.4%** (trial 2), and +13.0% (trial 10). The 2026-10-09 A/A
  reported "within 9.7%" from 12 trials; that was one sample, not a bound. Under the point
  rule in use until 2026-10-11 (WARN above 10%), trials 2 and 10 would have been false WARNs
  (2/12). Under the interval rule both are INCONCLUSIVE.

## gate_noise_x4.md: INVALID, kept as recorded (do not use)

Meant to test whether 4x the requests per run (136) narrows the interval. The laptop lost AC
power during this run: the manifest at the end says on battery (78%, GPU limit 30 W), the
battery fell from 90% to 78% between 23:12 and 23:26 UTC, and trials 3-6 took 148-157 s
instead of 131-132 s. When AC was lost cannot be determined, so no trial is usable. The SM
clock read 780 MHz throughout, but the power limit changed (80 W to 30 W). `gate_noise.py`
checked power only at start; since commit `767c2bf` it checks after every trial and stops.

Observation that motivated a re-run (not a result): the spread between runs of the same
side, not the number of requests in a run, dominates the interval, so more runs rather than
more requests per run is the likely fix. To be measured on AC.

## rq5: NOT RUN

`rq5.py` refused to start: "refusing to benchmark on battery". Repair under the interval
acceptance rule is therefore not measured yet; the most recent repair result remains
`2026-10-09-gate-warmup-v2/rq5.md` (point rule: 3/3 verified at -2.0% to +8.5% vs main).

# 2026-10-11: held-out set 4, Scan + Forge + Guard on three independent apps

Labels and the validation driver (with its expected outcomes) were committed in `f0fce9d`
before any scan. No scanner or reconstruction code changed between that commit and the
first scan, so `rq1_set4_first_scan.*` and `external_validation_first_run.*` are held-out
results. Apps (MIT, pinned commits in `bench/ground_truth/`): rag-postgres-openai-python
(FastAPI, pgvector hybrid RAG, OpenAI Agents SDK), tech-trends-chatbot (FastAPI + SSE, Redis
vector store, tool calling; a different author), openai-chat-backend-fastapi (minimal
Responses API backend).

## Scan (RQ1, `rq1_set4_first_scan.md`)

| category | held-out set 4 | for comparison: set 3 (2026-10-09) |
|---|---|---|
| LLM call sites | **2/9 recall, precision 1.00** | 8/9, precision 1.00 |
| routes | 10/13, precision 1.00 | |
| serving engine | 2/3 | |
| models | 0/6 | |
| retrievers, tools | 0/2, 0/2 | |
| attribute accuracy | 25/26 (empty scan: 15/21) | |

Why calls were missed (each is a construct the extractor does not resolve today):
- rag-postgres: all five generation calls go through the OpenAI Agents SDK
  (`Runner.run` / `Runner.run_streamed` with `Agent(instructions=...)`).
- openai-chat-backend: the client is held in a module-level dict
  (`clients["openai"].responses.create`).
- Models: values come from `os.getenv(..., default)` branches and pydantic-settings field
  defaults; none were read.

Prompts score low partly by labeling convention: the scanner reported the prompt files
(`prompts/answer.txt`) and per-call system slots; the labels name the Python attributes that
load the files. By the matching rule fixed before scoring these count as misses and false
positives; the labels were not changed after the scan. The report table was re-rendered
after a header fix (set 4 column was unlabeled); the numbers were verified identical.

## Source links, Forge, Guard (`external_validation*.md`)

- Source links: every file evidence of every finding resolves to the file and line range
  and contains its excerpt: 10 checked, 0 broken.
- Guard on synthetic PRs (expected = correct behavior, fixed before the run): docs-only and
  unrelated-code changes selected nothing, correct in 6/6. The prompt change (a per-request
  value prepended to the system prompt) was fully correct in 0/3: the prefix check and the
  prefix-instability signature were found in 2/3 apps, but the perf gate was not selected
  (no workflow reaches the prompt: the call sites above are missed, or the route reaches the
  LLM through `asyncio.create_task`); in rag-postgres the Agents SDK instructions were not
  recognized as a system prompt at all.
- Repair applicability: both strategies apply on openai-chat-backend and make the prompt
  prefix-stable again (re-analyzed); in tech-trends the system message is built in
  `__init__` and used elsewhere, which the strategies do not handle.
- Forge: plans 7 files on tech-trends (timeout test, prompt extraction, CI gate); 0 on the
  others, each with the reason (no harness: control flow before the messages are built /
  no route reaches the system-message builder; timeouts not installable on clients created
  inside factory functions). Forge refuses rather than guesses.
- Sandbox validation (run 2, `_sandbox_before_deps_fix`): failed on all three because the
  sandbox only installed a root `requirements.txt`; these apps keep requirements in
  `src/`, `src/backend/` (included from a root `requirements-dev.txt`) or Poetry only.
  **Fix (Furnace change, so later Forge-validation numbers on set 4 are "after fixes"):**
  the sandbox now installs the root `requirements-dev.txt` or `requirements.txt` with every
  `-r`/`-c` include that stays inside the repository (escapes refused, tested).
- Run 3 (`external_validation.md`, after the fix): openai-chat-backend's own test suite now
  runs in the sandbox, 5 passed and 1 failed (`test_chat_stream`, a snapshot mismatch on
  the unmodified code at the pinned commit: pre-existing, with `openai>=1.108.1`
  unpinned); Forge requires a green baseline, so no PR. rag-postgres: dependency install
  fails building psycopg2 from source in the slim image, and its tests need a live
  Postgres, which a network-less sandbox cannot provide. tech-trends: Poetry-only
  dependencies are not installed; no PR.

## What this says

Furnace generalizes where code calls an LLM SDK directly (set 3: 8/9) and degrades sharply
on indirection that is common in newer apps (agent frameworks, clients in containers,
background tasks): 2/9. It fails safe: no false positives on call sites or routes, no
wrong selections on unrelated PRs, Forge refusing with reasons, and no PR without a green
sandbox run. The next scanner work, measured on a new held-out set afterwards: Agents SDK
calls and instructions, subscripted clients, `create_task` edges, env/settings defaults.

## After fixes (set 4 is no longer held-out for these)

1. Sandbox dependency install (above): `external_validation_after_deps_fix.*`.
2. Guard selection: a detected prefix-instability signature now selects the benchmarks
   whose triggers include prompt changes even when no traced workflow reaches the prompt
   (`guardian/impact.py`, `lost_stable_prefix`). `external_validation.md`: the prompt
   scenario is correct in 2/3 apps (was 0/3), all scenarios 8/9; the remaining miss is
   rag-postgres, whose Agents SDK `instructions` are not recognized as a system prompt (a
   scanner gap, not a selection gap). F1's impact tests are unchanged.

## Scanner change for set-4 misses, measured on held-out set 5

Change (`code_intel/python_ast.py`): `Runner.run` / `run_streamed` / `run_sync` are LLM calls
when `Runner` comes from the `agents` package (OpenAI Agents SDK), with the model read from
the module-level `Agent(model=...)` passed to it (also across modules and for `Agent[Ctx](...)`);
a client held in a subscript (`clients["openai"].responses.create`) is matched by API suffix.
Negative tests: a local `Runner` class and an unrelated `registry["x"].get()` are not calls.

Set 5 (`openai/openai-cs-agents-demo`, labels committed in `f038d20` before the change;
baseline with the unchanged scanner in `rq1_set5_baseline_before_change.md`):
LLM call sites **0/3 -> 3/3 at precision 1.00**, models 0/2 -> 1/2 (the streamed call's agent
is chosen at runtime). Still missed: agent `instructions` are not extracted as prompts (0/8),
and the ChatKit server's route does not trace to the call (workflows 0/1). One app with three
call sites: evidence that the change generalizes beyond set 4, not a measurement of recall.

Regression check (`rq1_after_agents_sdk.json` vs `2026-10-09/rq1.json`): F1 and sets 1-3
unchanged in every category. Set 4 (no longer held-out): call sites 2/9 -> 9/9.

## Agent instructions as system prompts (after fixes; set 4 and 5 no longer held-out for this)

`Agent(instructions=<text>)` from the Agents SDK is analyzed like a system message (prefix
stability; one key per agent, `<scope>@<name>#system`); instruction *functions* are skipped;
module-level agents are included (module-level message dicts still are not). `self.X` /
`cls.X` in a prompt is shared text when X is a class attribute somewhere in the repository
(evaluated once at import). Results (`external_validation.md`, `rq1_after_agent_prompts.md`):
Guard on set 4 synthetic PRs now 9/9 correct, including rag-postgres's prompt regression;
the repair strategies do not handle agent instructions ("not applicable", reported), so
that app gets a correct diagnosis but no automated fix. Prompt P/R on sets 4-5 stays low by
the labeling convention noted above. F1 and sets 1-3 unchanged in every RQ1 category.
The driver now treats file-level evidence (excerpt = the path) as a file-existence check;
before, it reported one such link as broken.

# Campaign notes, 2026-10-06 (directory pinned with FURNACE_BENCH_DATE=2026-10-06)

- **Power.** The first RQ4 sweep ran on battery and was discarded (`rq4_battery_invalid/NOTES.md`).
  A second sweep on AC was cut short by a session end and discarded (`rq4_capped_partial/NOTES.md`).
- **GPU clock cap.** On AC, before and after a reboot, at 14% and at 56% battery, the laptop held
  the RTX 3050 Ti at **~780-830 MHz mean SM clock** under load (spot samples: P0, ~30-34 W, 80 W
  enforced power limit, no NVML throttle reason active; RQ4 telemetry recorded power peaks up to 64 W). The GPU's maximum is 2,100 MHz; the 2026-10-04 runs
  averaged 1,948 MHz and 72 W. This is a platform policy (OEM performance mode, Windows power
  mode or charger wattage), not something Furnace controls; it was not changed for this campaign.
- **Consequence.** The final RQ3, RQ4 and RQ5 results in this directory ran at that capped clock.
  Comparisons inside each RQ (configs, base vs PR vs repair) share the clock and are valid;
  absolute latencies are not comparable to the 2026-10-04 results. Each RQ4 run records its SM
  clock and AC state (`rq4/rq4.json` -> `clocks`, `clock_spread_pct`).
- **Host.** Development continued on the same machine during the GPU runs: editor, a Next.js dev
  server, the FastAPI dev server, the test suite (`poe check`, including short Docker sandbox tests)
  and Playwright screenshots. This adds CPU noise to client-side timing; repeats and revisions are
  interleaved so it spreads across configs rather than biasing one.

## Addendum 2026-10-09: the clock was not a power cap

Measured on the same laptop on AC, Windows power mode "Best performance", driver 592.82:
- A saturating load (fp16 4096x4096 matmul loop for 20 s in the vLLM image) ran at
  **1,830-1,852 MHz and 80 W** (24.7 TFLOPS); the only active clock-event reason was the normal
  80 W software power limit.
- The lab vLLM serving Qwen2.5-0.5B under 16-48 concurrent requests ran at **780 MHz, ~30 W**,
  utilization ~80%, with **"Idle" as the only active clock-event reason**: no power, thermal or
  power-brake throttling.

So "capped" above is the wrong word: the driver chose ~780 MHz for this light, bursty serving
load. The 2026-10-04 vLLM runs averaged 1,948 MHz; what made the driver boost then and not now is
not identified. The consequence paragraph stands unchanged: comparisons inside each RQ share the
clock; absolute latencies are at this clock. `scripts/preflight.py --load` reports the clock and
the active reasons before a demo.

2026-10-11 (UTC), after a reboot: under the same vLLM load the driver chose **1,957-1,972 MHz at
up to 60 W** (only the "Idle" reason active). The clock this load gets is a driver state that
changed across reboots. A live run at that clock was 32-48% faster at p95 TTFT than the same run
at 780 MHz (`../2026-10-11-live-clock/NOTES.md`).

**1. The perf gate was biased, so RQ5's "3/3 verified" does not hold.** Without a warmup wave, the first requests after the GPU sat idle took ~200 ms instead of ~65 ms and set each run's p95; the base revision, measured first, read ~2.4x slower. An A/A test (main vs itself) showed differences up to 60%; with a warmup wave the A/A noise is at most 9.7% (`2026-10-09/gate_noise.md`). Re-measured, R1 costs **+905% to +1,004%** p95 TTFT (not +336% to +414%), and the repair reported below ("move to the end of the user message") is **+40% to +50%** over main and is blocked: 0/3 (`2026-10-09-gate-warmup/`).

**2. Current result** (`2026-10-09-gate-warmup-v2/`): the repair loop now tries a second strategy, logging the per-request values instead of sending them: **3/3 verified at -2.0% to +8.5% vs main**, prefix-cache hit 98% -> 98%, 3/3 full-suite audits clean.

**3. "Capped GPU clock" was the wrong word.** The laptop GPU reaches 1,850 MHz under a saturating load; under this serving load the driver holds ~780 MHz with no throttle reason active (NOTES.md, 2026-10-09 addendum).

RQ1, RQ2 and RQ4 do not use the perf gate. RQ3's perf-gate noise figures came from the biased gate; its regression recall did not depend on them.

The gate now decides on a 95% interval (hierarchical bootstrap over runs and requests): on the same 12 trials, 0 false WARN or BLOCK, 7 PASS, 5 INCONCLUSIVE (reported as such, never as a pass), and the interval contained the true difference in 12/12 (`docs/furnacebench.md`, "The perf gate's decision rule"). # R1 end-to-end repair with a real performance gate (2026-10-04)

**Scenario.** `fixtures/scenarios/f1_scenarios.py::r1_dynamic_head`: a PR prepends
`f"Request {uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]} at {datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()}\n"` to F1's system prompt.

**What ran** (`furnace.guardian.repair.loop.repair_prefix_instability`, total ~38 s):

1. Harness generated from F1's own `/chat` handler (`furnace_harness.py`).
2. Regression test written first, calibrated on the base revision (two different requests
   share 3,954 leading characters on base; 15 on the PR head; threshold 3,558).
3. Reproduced in the Docker sandbox: the test FAILS on the PR head and PASSES on base.
4. Localized to 2 hunks in `app/prompts.py::build_messages`.
5. Candidate from the deterministic rule `prefix_stability.move_dynamic_to_suffix`
   (keeps the request id and timestamp, moves them after the static text).
6. Validated in the sandbox: regression test passes, existing tests pass.
7. Performance gate: prompts rendered from each revision's own code (34 unique questions,
   unique per-run reference appended so no request repeats), replayed by furnace-bench at
   concurrency 8, 64 output tokens, against vLLM 0.30.0 serving Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-AWQ on
   an RTX 3050 Ti Laptop GPU.

| revision | TTFT p95 | vs base | prefix-cache hit | SLO goodput (TTFT ≤ 500 ms) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| base | 579.3 ms | – | 96.1% | 6.25 req/s |
| PR head | 1,472.7 ms | +154.2% (block) | 0.0% | 0.93 req/s |
| repair | 647.5 ms | +11.8% (warn) | 80.8% | 5.64 req/s |

Policy: warn above +10%, block above +25% (p95 TTFT vs base).

**Residual.** The repair keeps the per-request id inside the system message (at its end), which
still prevents sharing of the retrieved-context block that follows it; hence 80.8% vs 96.1% hits
and +11.8% p95. Moving the dynamic values to the end of the *user* message would remove this, at
the cost of a larger change to the PR's intent. Not implemented yet.

**Caveats.** One run per revision, n = 34 at a single concurrency level. FurnaceBench RQ5 will
repeat this with 3 repetitions and report spread.

Artifacts: `repair.patch` (fix + harness + regression test), `attempt.json` (RepairAttempt),
`perf.json` (gate verdicts and full furnace-bench reports for all three revisions).

# R1 de-risk: shared prompt prefix vs. dynamic head (2026-10-04)

**Question.** Is the planned primary regression (a per-request value prepended to the
system prompt, which defeats prefix caching) measurable on the laptop GPU?

**Setup.** vLLM 0.30.0, Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (served as `lab`), RTX 3050 Ti Laptop
4 GB, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.70 --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 32`,
prefix caching on (vLLM default). furnace-bench closed loop, 60 measured + 8 warmup
requests per level, fixed 128 output tokens (`ignore_eos`), streaming, seed 1234/1235.
Both workloads: ~1,720 prompt tokens per request (measured from server usage).

- `21111ede417c` `f1-shape-prefix-stable`: 1,000-token system prompt shared by all requests.
- `91474182777a` `f1-shape-dynamic-head`: no shared prefix (what a dynamic head causes).

**Result (single repeat; p95 with 95% bootstrap CI).**

| c | TTFT p95 stable | TTFT p95 dynamic head | SLO goodput (TTFT ≤ 500 ms) req/s | prefix-cache hit |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 70 [67, 72] | 119 [117, 120] | 0.95 → 0.91 | 58.7% → 0.9% |
| 4 | 213 [207, 214] | 409 [388, 413] | 3.01 → 2.48 | 58.7% → 0.9% |
| 8 | 374 [341, 397] | 648 [476, 875] | 4.78 → 3.18 | 58.7% → 0.9% |
| 16 | 752 [521, 755] | 1,577 [1,041, 1,712] | 5.83 → 3.01 | 58.7% → 0.9% |

The measured hit rate (58.7%) matches the expected shared fraction (1,000 / ~1,717 = 58.2%).

**Caveats.** One repeat on a laptop GPU (thermal/clock variance not yet characterized);
at c=16 the TTFT *median* is unchanged (369 vs 367 ms) while the tail doubles. The
FurnaceBench RQ4/RQ5 runs will use 3 repeats and report spread.

**Decision.** R1 stays the primary repair scenario.

**Setup.** F1 (`fixtures/apps/support-rag-py`, unmodified prompt) served by vLLM 0.30.0 on an
RTX 3050 Ti Laptop. `scripts/traffic.py --rate 2 --repeat 2 --seed 7`: 88 questions (68 documented
facts, 12 out-of-scope, 8 needing a human), Poisson arrivals. Traces are the app's own call log.

**Deterministic checks on the traces** (`furnace.evals.runner`):

| model | citation_required PASS | TTFT ≤ 500 ms PASS |
|---|---:|---:|
| Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (fp16) | 3 / 89 | 88 / 89 |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-AWQ | 9 / 88 | 87 / 88 |

(The 0.5B run includes one extra manual smoke request.) Neither model uses the documented
"I could not find that in the Kilnworks documentation." phrasing for out-of-scope questions (0 / 12).

**Failures observed that need a semantic judge (not caught by deterministic checks):**
- 1.5B-AWQ, "What is the price of the Enterprise plan?" -> invents an Enterprise plan at
  "$79 per month ... up to 5 kilns" (no such plan; $79 is the Workshop plan, 12 kilns).
- 1.5B-AWQ, "My kiln smells like burning plastic during firing" -> advises removing the safety
  sensors, which the system prompt explicitly forbids.
- 0.5B, "Can safety interlocks be disabled remotely?" -> "Yes, safety interlocks cannot be disabled..."

**Serving trade-off on the 4 GB GPU:** KV cache 120,848 tokens (0.5B fp16) vs 24,672 tokens
(1.5B AWQ) at `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.70`.

**Workload fingerprint** (0.5B traces, exact Qwen tokenizer): prompt p50 965 / p95 980 tokens,
system prompt 849 tokens, output p50 25 / p95 162, prefix reuse 93.5% (one 857-token group
covering 100% of requests), arrival 2.06 req/s with CV 0.98 (generator: Poisson at 2.0 req/s),
peak concurrency 5. The Blueprint's 4-chars/token estimate of the system prompt (~982 tokens)
was 16% high.
